rationale: My round-2 ask is ADDRESSED in full and well (classification below): the release row carries both carve-outs with the exact citation chain I derived, a legitimate redesign leg is posed to plan time alongside OQ-3 rather than decided, and release is recorded as the second deterministic #248 route with R3.2/AC-5(i)-(ii) running on both fixtures. Charter fidelity otherwise remains sound at round 3: settled facts intact, OQ-1/2/3/5 still genuinely open (the round-2 G7 per-arm tagging of AC-6/AC-7 strengthens OQ-1's openness), the #255 boundary unchanged and crisp, and the new R6.7/AC-15 is legitimate in-cluster growth (#187's scoped-selection honesty), not scope drift. However, the round-2 G6 mechanism replacement was not propagated into the spec's own scope fences, leaving a direct internal contradiction: R3.3 now unconditionally obligates EVERY mindspec_phase writer to take the new lock — enumerating plan approve's plan.go:455 write and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write — while In Scope still lists internal/approve/plan.go as touched 'only if OQ-3 resolves against the stored-implement write' (now false), and the impl approve/adopt write sites (re-derived at the tree: internal/approve/impl.go, e.g. the derived-reconcile write at :578 plus the done write, and internal/approve/adopt.go:424) appear nowhere in In Scope or the Impacted-Domains parenthetical. A plan or bead reading the scope fence would treat R3.3's writer rollout as conditional or partially out-of-bounds, which quietly weakens the very concurrency fix G6 demanded. This is the same propagation defect class as my round-2 finding (a group fix not run through the document's other load-bearing sections), it is unambiguous, and the repair is small — hence REQUEST_CHANGES, narrow, without hard_block.
concrete_changes_required: Propagate R3.3's unconditional writer-lock obligation into the scope fences: (i) In Scope — replace 'internal/approve/plan.go (only if OQ-3 resolves against the stored-implement write)' with an entry reflecting that plan.go's mindspec_phase write takes the R3.3 lock regardless of OQ-3 (the OQ-3 conditional now governs only whether the WRITTEN VALUE changes), and add the impl approve/impl adopt write surfaces (internal/approve/impl.go, internal/approve/adopt.go) that R3.3's enumeration obligates; (ii) Impacted Domains — update the internal/approve/** parenthetical the same way. Derived at 9ac301ee: R3.3 names 'every other mindspec_phase writer … plan approve's write at plan.go:455 … and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write', and the tree shows those terminal-verb writes live at internal/approve/impl.go (derived-reconcile write at :578, the done write, plus a pre-080 backfill path near :274) and internal/approve/adopt.go:424 — neither file is in scope today.

Pin R3.3's writer enumeration the way this spec pins every other drift-prone list (R5.1's enumeration test, AC-14's total classification): 'enumerated at this base' prose names ONE impl-approve 'terminal write', but internal/approve/impl.go contains at least two distinct mindspec_phase writes (:578 reconcile-to-derived and the mindspec_phase=done write) plus a backfill path — an unenumerated writer silently bypasses the lock and reopens the race AC-5(v) claims closed. Require a test (grep-anchored or seam-anchored) asserting every MergeMetadata call site writing mindspec_phase sits inside the lock's critical section, or at minimum correct the enumeration to the true write-site set and state the anti-drift mechanism.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: R3.3's unconditional writer-lock obligation contradicts the In-Scope conditional on plan.go and omits the impl approve/adopt write surfaces
findings.detail: Round-2 G6 replaced the repair-race mechanism with a lock 'held … by repair phase and by every other mindspec_phase writer (enumerated at this base: plan approve's write at plan.go:455, complete's step-6.5 sync, release's step-6.5 sync …, and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write)'. That makes plan.go, impl.go/adopt.go edits mandatory under every OQ-3/OQ-1 outcome. But In Scope still reads 'internal/approve/plan.go (only if OQ-3 resolves against the stored-implement write)' — now false — and lists neither internal/approve/impl.go nor internal/approve/adopt.go, whose mindspec_phase writes I re-derived at the tree (impl.go:578 reconcile-to-derived and the done write; adopt.go:424). The Impacted-Domains internal/approve parenthetical carries the same stale conditional. The fences a plan and its bead panels enforce would exclude work R3.3 requires. Additionally, R3.3's prose enumeration undercounts impl approve's write sites (one 'terminal write' named; at least two writes plus a backfill path exist), and unlike R5.1/AC-14 the enumeration has no anti-drift pin — an unenumerated writer bypasses the lock and reopens the race AC-5(v) declares closed.
